about: Hand audit of the Haiku 5.5 test sweep 20261117T192758Z (33 runs: the 11 test scenarios x 3), by Claude, blind: written from each run's transcript only (its alarm prompt, tool output, and Hypothesis, shown by a viewer that reads the transcript and nothing else), before the checker, the rubric, or grading ran on this sweep, and without reading the user's three label files (24d99e4). diagnosis: right = names the injected fault's cause and mechanism and blames nothing else; partly = one of those missing; wrong = blames something else; none = no answer. slips: claims past the run's own tool output, each {target, kind, complaint, note}. target: e<n> an evidence item, s<n> a root_cause sentence (numbered by evals.audit.sentences), i<n> an inference. kind: strict = the output contradicts it or never showed it; loose = roughly true but past the data. complaint: contradicted; outside_read (about rows, lines, or a period its read doesn't cover); miscited (cites what doesn't exist or isn't what it says); unsupported (no evidence carries it). One label per target and complaint; a run with no slips has []. Kept from the 2026-11-13 audit: strict covers a value outside the rows or lines read, a wrong count or sum, a first or only event claimed from a read that left older lines out, a value given the wrong time or source, and a share with the wrong denominator; a claim about a period the run never read is strict (the user's call, 2026-11-13); loose covers an 'about', 'roughly', or 'near' hiding a wider range, a vague scope, and a span rounded beyond the read; claims the run makes in not_checked are not labeled. New in this audit: (1) Older changes: a claim that a metric stayed flat or clean, had no effect, or showed no change, or that a symptom began only at a time, offered to rule out an older change whose aftermath the run never read, is strict outside_read. A plain onset claim the read shows is not a slip, nor is an argument from timing alone, nor a claim scoped to the rows the run read. (2) Typed items are literal: a lines list cites only its lines (c368a0a), so lines [1, 20] is two lines; a range's low and high must be the least and greatest values in its window or cited lines, and either one wrong is strict contradicted (a range written in prose with 'about', 'roughly', or 'near' is loose); a none must hold no record in its window (one that does is strict contradicted), and a none window that starts or ends exactly on a record is loose contradicted. (3) A source the run never read (m2 when it read only m1) is strict miscited, whatever the values. (4) Form-only faults are not labeled when every stated fact is in the cited record or line: a value under a wrong or nonexistent column (ts, timestamp, value, kind, version), or a compound value such as 'POOL_MAX_SIZE 20->2' or '1.43.0->1.42.0'; a changed key as the column (POOL_MAX_SIZE: '20->2') is the schema's own instruction. (5) Uncited but true: an inference whose rests_on doesn't carry it, or a true figure no item cites, is not a slip if the run's output shows it. (6) Durations are checked against the deploy records' timestamps; one further off than its 'about' allows (about 2 hours for 1 h 26 min, about 75 minutes for 1 h 34 min) is strict contradicted, and a rounding such as about four hours for 3 h 46 min is not labeled. (7) Traffic named as a contributing factor rather than the cause doesn't make a diagnosis partly. (8) A '-' metrics row (no payments calls that minute) doesn't contradict 'timeouts are 0 in every row'.
